title: Meteors, Morph Layouts, Ruby Type, Cursor FX & CSS Ratings
description: Five live drops: an Aceternity-style meteor shower, a persistent grid/masonry/list morph gallery, CSS ruby annotations, a cursor-effects lab, and a zero-JS :has() rating widget.

drops.title: Meteor Shower
drops.description: Diagonal meteor trails stream across a twinkling starfield and bend toward the cursor; click for a 14-meteor burst.
drops.concept: Aceternity's Meteor Effect and Shooting Stars components popularized diagonal falling-star trails as a background accent. This drop reimplements the technique from scratch in Canvas 2D, adding cursor-seeking trajectories and a click-triggered burst so the effect reads as a small interactive scene rather than a static background.
drops.source: Inspired by ui.aceternity.com's 'Meteor Effect' and 'Shooting Stars and Stars Background' components

interaction.mouse: Meteors bend toward the cursor as they fall
interaction.click: Spawns a 14-meteor burst at the click point
interaction.touch: Tap anywhere to trigger a burst

drops.title: Layout Morph Gallery
drops.description: Twelve tiles tween their own left/top/width/height between grid, masonry, list and featured layouts — nothing unmounts.
drops.concept: Codrops' June 2026 piece on persistent WebGPU page transitions describes a 'Keep / Remove / Add' rule: elements present before and after a transition tween their bounds directly instead of being destroyed and recreated. This drop reimplements that idea in plain CSS transform/position transitions (no WebGPU) applied to four classic layout algorithms — grid, masonry, list, and an asymmetric featured layout — so switching modes reads as one continuous rearrangement.
drops.source: Reimplements the persistent-element transition technique from Codrops' WebGPU page-transitions tutorial

interaction.mouse: Click a layout mode button to morph all tiles

drops.title: Annotated Type
drops.description: Click any word to attach a native CSS ruby gloss and choose a text-emphasis mark style — dot, circle, sesame, or open triangle.
drops.concept: CSS ruby annotations (traditionally used for East Asian pronunciation guides) and text-emphasis marks are underused outside their original context, but the CSS Ruby Annotation Layout Module makes them a genuinely native way to add inline glosses or emphasis to any Latin-script text. This drop turns both into a live authoring tool: select a word, type a gloss, pick an emphasis mark, and see it render instantly with the real <ruby>/<rt> elements and text-emphasis CSS.
drops.source: Built on the CSS Ruby Annotation Layout Module and text-emphasis property

interaction.mouse: Click a word to select it, then apply a gloss + emphasis style
interaction.touch: Tap words to select on mobile

drops.title: Cursor FX Lab
drops.description: Three canvas cursor effects — particle trail, magnetic ribbon, and ripple burst — switchable live from a glass panel.
drops.concept: A wave of small 'cursor effects showcase' repos has emerged, collecting dozens of canvas-driven mouse interactions behind a single switcher UI. This drop reimplements three of the most common effect families from first principles — velocity-based particle emission, a spring-chained ribbon that lags behind the pointer, and expanding ripple rings on click — each built independently rather than ported from source.
drops.source: Inspired by the cursor-effects showcase format of Felix-au/CursorX-Interactive-Cursor-Effects

interaction.mouse: Move to drive the active effect
interaction.click: Ripple mode bursts rings on click/tap
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the canvas

drops.title: Rate & React
drops.description: Star, thumbs, and emoji-mood rating widgets — all visual state is pure CSS via radio inputs and :has(), no JS required for the look.
drops.concept: No-JavaScript star ratings built from radio inputs and the general sibling combinator are a well-known CSS trick; this drop extends the pattern with a modern touch by using :has() to make each card's border and glow react the moment any input inside it becomes checked, without a single line of JS driving the visuals. Three distinct rating shapes (stars, binary thumbs, five-point emoji mood) show the technique isn't limited to stars.
drops.source: Technique from Kate Rose Morley's CSS star rating widget, extended with :has()

interaction.mouse: Hover to preview, click to select
interaction.click: Selecting any widget lights up its card border via :has()
